correctness.rationale: For a defect leaf v attached to w, all faces containing vw are exactly {v,w} union a subset of N_F(w) minus v, irrespective of cycles elsewhere. Choose x another neighbor of w; pairing lower faces without x to uppers with x in descending subset-size order leaves each lower face free, with exactly 2^(deg_F(w)-2) pairs. After these all vw-containing faces, and only these, are gone, giving exactly X_{F-vw}. Iterated pruning of a forest retains one edge per nontrivial component; collapsing the two full-shore simplices in the matching case yields the claimed integral sphere/circle-wedge types. Standalone checker directly verified 1,399 intermediate free-face pairs over 640 examples and mod-two homology for 440 forest examples; finite tests are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The universal relative simple-homotopy collapse is a structural invariance theorem for arbitrary missing-edge patterns of complete bipartite graphs, not a one-off homology count. It yields a natural complete forest classification independent of branching and a safe reduction to the cyclic core for all bipartite defect graphs, preserving all homotopy-invariant information. An isolated edge provides the sharp boundary, because its deletion changes connectivity. The result is relevant to reducing topological computations under graph edge faults, even though it does not classify general cyclic cores.
